name: ACME Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (CFI-G)

sources.note: PSI-159 search record, field 'Flight Platform': International Space Station (ISS); Project Type 'Microgravity Investigation'
Challenge brief frames the combustion investigations as microgravity studies aboard the ISS

objective.value: Determine the conditions under which cool diffusion flames occur for propane, n-butane and n-pentane, in normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames, over a broad range of stoichiometric mixture fraction (Zst), adiabatic flame temperature (Tad), flow rate and pressure; support the ISS tests with CFD simulations, identify a chemical-kinetics mechanism that matches the measurements, and disseminate the results.

sources.note: PSI-159 detail record, field 'objective' (local data/source/psi/PSI-159.json): determine conditions for cool diffusion flames in propane/n-butane/n-pentane, normal and inverse flames, wide Zst/Tad/flow range; CFD support; kinetic mechanism
ACME overview: observe quasi-steady spherical cool diffusion flames on porous burners with gaseous fuel; support cool-flame kinetics modelling
PSI-159 detail record, fields 'objective' and 'researchImpacts': the study determines cool-diffusion-flame conditions and develops a chemical-kinetics mechanism - fundamental combustion science
ACME overview: ACME is fundamental microgravity research whose secondary objective is spacecraft fire prevention; CFI-G itself is framed as cool-flame kinetics

safety_functions.note: No source labels CFI-G with prevention, detection or suppression; classified fundamental.

The investigation is fundamental cool-flame kinetics rather than a suppression or detection test.

notes: Local PSI record read: data/source/psi/PSI-159.json and PSI-159.search.json. Per-test tables are PSI-159_Experimental table_CFI-G_Normal Flames.csv and PSI-159_Experimental table_CFI-G_Inverse Flames.csv; their ranges were read via data/source/psi/tables/conditions.json, not the CSVs directly.

O2: the brief states up to 85% oxygen (burner-supplied O2/N2 mixture). The PSI table agrees - max XO2 = 85% (Inverse Flames table, range 12-85%); the Normal Flames table chamber XO2 is lower (~18-40%). No conflict with the brief. o2_percent left at its seed value; scripts/psi_apply_conditions.py overwrites it from the table.
pressure_psi left at the seed value (unknown) for scripts/psi_apply_conditions.py, which fills it from the table (PSI-159 approx p: 7.185-48.006 psi over 1194 rows).
airflow left unknown: the PSI tables list fuel/oxidizer mass flow rates (mg/s), not an air velocity; no airflow value is stated in the sources read.

Data set is very large (totalFileSize 2,085,592,429,259 bytes = ~2.09 TB across 3756 files) and was not downloaded. Only names, counts and sizes from the PSI 'added' list were recorded: mostly .zip image/converted-data archives (987), .txt as-run files (1022), .csv (680), .mdipsug instrument data (610), .ts video segments (336), .log (22), plus 93 PDFs (reports, engineering docs, test sheets), 1 xlsx (ACME Chamber Calculator), and 1 representative .png/.jpg.

psi.nasa.gov is a JavaScript page the web tool cannot render; no PSI web page was consulted and none is claimed. The NASA ACME overview PDF (one web fetch) was read for hardware/diagnostics/context and states no CFI-G O2 or pressure, so it neither supports nor contradicts the condition figures.
PSI-159 publications: two peer-reviewed papers listed; added to 'publications' with DOI links. PSI record DOI (dataset) is 10.60555/cyt1-kh64.
